chapters.title: What goes out the door
chapters.summary: One base résumé, tuned by audience.
paragraphs: One base résumé, with the emphasis shifted by the kind of role: software, IT or analyst.
Every cover letter started from one base and was written to one posting. Any number without backing came off the page, even the strongest line.

chapters.title: The projects are deliverables
chapters.summary: Things that ran, with evidence attached.
paragraphs: Catch 5 was the card game we played at home, built as an iPhone app and checked by 264 automated tests.
Drive Score rebuilt the data pipeline from the internship, running on sample trips. Each project showed the result and the decisions behind it, not just the code.

chapters.title: Selection, not chasing
paragraphs: Searches ran more than one way, because each found roles the other missed. Every posting was read for warning signs: constant on-call, ticket quotas, being the only IT person.

The shortlist held 23 roles: 10 ready to send, five to check on schedule, five to check on fit and three closed. The bar for accepting stayed narrow: predictable hours and a team that supported people.

chapters.title: The instrument
chapters.summary: Built the scoreboard before drawing conclusions.
paragraphs: tracker-digest, a small purpose-built tool, read the application spreadsheet and listed the follow-ups owed.
The scoreboard kept the search honest. Decisions came from the numbers, not from one quiet week.

chapters.title: The intangibles
chapters.summary: The intangibles counted more, not less.
paragraphs: Explaining a technical idea to someone without the background. Reconciling a cash drawer to zero. Writing things down so the next person could pick them up.
Teaching, restaurants and a county golf course built those habits. They were the half of the job AI did not touch.
